title: Fragmented JSON reassembly protocol for streaming structured outputs
creator: Lina Chen
description: Problem: Clients using streaming structured outputs (JSON) encounter partial objects, escaped characters crossing buffer boundaries, and truncation mid-token. We need a pragmatic protocol that lets the server stream valid, recoverable fragments to the client while preserving backward compatibility with older SDKs and enabling safe retries. This ticket designs a reassembly and retry protocol, edge-case handling heuristics, and an implementation checklist for runtime + SDK changes.
acceptance_criteria: Define wire-level framing tokens so receivers can resynchronize after truncated chunks (both new clients and best-effort for legacy clients)
Server emits explicit fragment metadata for each chunk: fragment_id, seq, is_last, byte_checksum, optional resume_token (base64)
SDKs (Python/Node/Go) implement reassembly using the fragment metadata and fall back to tolerant JSON repair when metadata absent
If a stream is truncated, server produces a deterministic partial-JSON repair heuristic and a non-ambiguous error code so apps can decide to retry or abort

E2E tests covering: escaped quotes crossing chunk boundaries, unicode multi-byte codepoints split across chunks, function-calling structured payloads split mid-argument, and resume after transient connection failure
tech_notes: Framing model: prefix each logical chunk with a 1-line JSON header followed by a newline and the raw chunk payload. Header example (single-line): {\"fragment_id\":\"f-abc123\",\"seq\":1,\"is_last\":false,\"resume_token\":\"c29tZXRva2Vu\",\"checksum\":\"sha256:...\"}

Recovery heuristics: when header absent (legacy clients) try to reconstruct via
      - greedy bracket matching with escape-awareness
      - UTF-8 boundary repair (drop partial codepoint + mark repaired)
      - if spare fragments exist, attempt patching using incremental-json-patch (see ENG-15021)

Resume semantics: resume_token is opaque and monotonic; resumption request should include last-applied seq and token. Server validates and streams remaining fragments. Idempotency guaranteed by fragment_id+seq checks.

Truncation policy: runtime will try to finish the current JSON object by emitting a synthetic closing tail when the generation hits model max-tokens or connection is severed due to timeout. That tail is emitted as a special fragment with header field truncated=true and an error_code that maps to retriable | non-retriable.

Backwards compatibility: older SDKs will ignore single-line header lines if they don't start with the expected prefix and fall into repair heuristics. New SDKs will parse header and prefer resume_token-based resumption.
Observability: add metrics: fragmented_stream_rate, malformed_fragment_rate, resume_success_rate, avg_reassembly_ms. Dashboards to tie malformed_fragment spikes to model/version and infra region.
Security: resume_token must be short-lived and HMACed per-connection. Avoid embedding PII in headers. Security review required (see security_review_required).
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting — decided on one-line JSON header + raw payload approach to minimize parser changes for legacy SDKs. Attendees: Lina (owner), Miguel, Asha (runtime), Rahul (SDK), Priya (SEC).
2026-02-20: Prototype server streaming header+payload implemented in runtime branch feat/stream-frag. Initial tests show 0.9ms extra latency per chunk for header generation.
2026-02-24: SDK PoC: Node SDK parses header and resumes successfully in simulated TCP cut. Python SDK fallback repair implemented but needs edge-case tests.
2026-03-02: Discovered unicode bug: multi-byte characters split across chunks caused UTF-8 decode errors in old clients. Added UTF-8 boundary detection and repair; tests added.
2026-03-08: Sync with Console team: coordinate rollouts and dashboard tiles for malformed_fragment_rate. Plan: feature-flagged rollout for 2 weeks then enable by default.
2026-03-10: Design review completed. Miguel opened PRs: GH #redwood/runtime PR 5212 and GH #redwood/sdk-node PR 891. Security checklist created. Next: implement automated resume e2e tests in CI.
decisions: Use an explicit header line (single-line JSON) before each chunk instead of inline binary framing — chosen for readability in logs and easier incremental adoption.
Resume token = opaque base64 HMAC(payload_metadata + expiry) — server validates to avoid replay.
When model-generated content truncates mid-object, emit a truncated fragment with truncated=true and error_code=TRUNCATED_STREAM to allow callers to choose retry or accept partial data.
Legacy clients get best-effort repair; we will not break them by default. New SDKs default to strict reassembly and will expose a tolerant flag for compatibility.
review_comments: Asha (runtime): header generation adds CPU overhead; microbenchmark shows 0.9ms/chunk — acceptable but we should batch header creation on hot paths.
Rahul (SDK): Node SDK resume flow needs rate-limit protections to prevent client loops — adding exponential backoff and max-resume-attempts=3.
Priya (SEC): resume_token lifetime must not exceed 30s for public API. Also recommend HMAC using per-tenant key and rotate keys monthly.
Product (Jae Park): prefer visible error codes for customers. Add mapping table for TRUNCATED_STREAM => actionable message in Console and SDKs.
